title: Monthly Late Charges on Past-Due Fee Invoices of the Contingency Placement Agreements and Their Booking Instrument
content:
Each monthly late charge on a past-due fee invoice of an agreement under the Contingency Placement Agreements is figured under the late-charge rule, one charge for each full calendar month the invoice stays unpaid after its late-charge start. A full calendar month after a late-charge start runs from that day to the same day of the next month, or to that month's last day where the same day does not exist.

## Business effect of booking

Booking a month's late charge adds one late-charge entry, dated the day of booking and tied to the named invoice, to the agreement's client money history, and raises the fees the client owes Ridgeline on that agreement by the same amount. The charge then appears in the agreement's money history under that invoice and in its fees owed. Each booking is one month's charge on one invoice.

## Instrument: `assess_invoice_late_charge_7a6464d6`

**Capability.** One call books one month's late charge on one past-due fee invoice of a creditor client's contingency placement agreement, with the business effect stated above.

**How it is invoked.** The tool is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `assess_invoice_late_charge_7a6464d6` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `agreement_id` | the placement agreement reference number (agreement id) of the agreement the invoice was raised on, read from the placement agreement lookup | identifier, as the lookup shows it |
| `invoice_number` | the fee invoice number exactly as it appears on the invoice entry in the agreement's client money history (and as the client reads it from the invoice) | verbatim: copied character for character with its letters, digits and hyphen, no change of any kind |
| `late_charge_amount` | the month's late charge | USD, always positive, rounded to the nearest cent (2 decimal places) before it is passed |

**Return.** A text receipt of a dictionary with:

- `entry_id` — the reference of the new client money entry;
- `agreement_id` — the agreement charged;
- `invoice_number` — the invoice the charge is tied to;
- `entry_type` — always `client_late_charge_assessed`;
- `amount` — the charge booked, USD to 2 decimal places;
- `entry_date` — today, YYYY-MM-DD;
- `fees_owed_after` — the agreement's fees owed once the charge is added, USD to 2 decimal places.

Receiving the receipt means the late charge is booked.

## Full calendar months — hypothetical dates

| Late-charge start | First full calendar month runs to |
|---|---|
| 15 March | 15 April |
| 31 January, in a year whose February has 28 days | 28 February |
| 30 April | 30 May |

An invoice whose late-charge start was 15 March and which is still unpaid on 16 June has stayed unpaid for three full calendar months after its late-charge start (to 15 April, 15 May and 15 June); one late charge is figured for each of those three months.
